title: One step of the move sweep
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $E$ inject optional $\Gamma$-symbols into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits, and let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an injection. For a finite Turing machine $M$ over $\Gamma$, a binary word $x$, a configuration $c$ on its letterwise $e$-image, an action $a$ of $M$, and a move-sweep counter $r\in\{0,\ldots,N+1\}$ with $r\ne0$, one step of the simulator from the move-sweep configuration at counter $r$ yields the move-sweep configuration at counter $r-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $\Gamma$ is finite and has decidable equality
$E$ is an injection from optional symbols to blocks
$e$ is an injection from bits to $\Gamma$
$M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$c$ is a configuration on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$
replaced:
For a counter $r \neq 0$, one transition of the binary block-code simulator applied to
the move-sweep configuration (source configuration $c$, source action $a$) at counter
$r$ yields the move-sweep configuration at counter $r-1$: each work head advances one
cell in its pending direction.
